description:
/fly HUD speed readout shows 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet missions (Galileo, Voyager 2, New Horizons, Dawn) throughout the interplanetary cruise phase

Expected: The HUD speed readout should show a numeric km/s value for every mission, including outer-planet destinations, for every position along the trajectory

Acceptance criteria:
- heliocentricSpeed(rAu, aTransferAu) must not return NaN for any rAu > 0, aTransferAu > 0 [code-invariant: sqrt of negative is NaN; user-facing HUD must never show NaN]
- When the vis-viva radicand (2/rAu - 1/aTransferAu) is negative (i.e., rAu > 2 * aTransferAu), heliocentricSpeed falls back to the local circular orbital speed sqrt(mu / rAu), scaled to km/s via AU_PER_YR_TO_KMS [reporter: Reporter answer: 'It should fall back to the local circular orbital speed at that radius, sqrt(mu / r)']
- The /fly HUD displays a non-NaN numeric km/s value for every outer-planet mission catalog entry (Galileo, Voyager 2, New Horizons, Dawn) across the full trajectory time range [reporter: Bug report: 'the HUD speed readout just says NaN km/s the whole way']

Domain facts:
- static/data/planets.json: Earth a=1.0 AU, Mars a=1.52366 AU → (1+1.52366)/2 = 1.26183 AU is the hardcoded aTransfer for all non-Moon missions
- The e2e render-validation test (tests/e2e/fly-render-validation.spec.ts) only exercises Moon and Mars cases — no outer-planet missions in the CASES array — so the bug is invisible to CI
- The per-mission validation test (src/lib/fly-physics-validation.test.ts) only validates Mars missions and uses the same hardcoded aTransfer
